detail:
Measured on an idle Apple M5 / 32 GB / node v26.8.2, five tiers, events spread over 24 month shards, via scripts/measure/corpus.ts. Full report: docs/reports/2026-09-resource-measurements.md.

  tier   append p50   append p95   events/s
  1,000   11.9 ms      13.1 ms      85.3
  2,000   13.7 ms      22.2 ms      67.0
  4,000   19.9 ms      31.2 ms      48.3
  8,000   26.9 ms      55.6 ms      36.0
 16,000   48.9 ms      77.8 ms      21.0

Least-squares log-log fit: p50 ≈ 0.323 × n^0.50. Per-append cost is a function of history length, so writing a corpus costs O(n^1.5), not O(n).

Consequences:
- C28 A25 targets p95 < 100 ms for durable local capture. Measured p95 at 16k is 77.8 ms. Using the measured p95/p50 ratio (1.59), the fit puts the crossing at roughly 35,000 events — reachable in ordinary use by a store that never truncates.
- 100k was NOT attempted to completion: the fit projects p50 ≈ 108 ms and ≈ 3.0 hours single-threaded on this machine. The largest tier completed is 16,000. Reported as projected, never as measured.
- Migration and bulk-import throughput inherit the same curve.

Ruled out as causes (do not re-derive):
- Month sharding. The store shards by occurred_at.slice(0,7). Piling a whole corpus into ONE directory (--single-shard) was measured FASTER at 1k than spreading over 24 months (p50 10.9 ms vs 13.2 ms); spreading costs a little on append and a lot on rebuild. I initially wrote this up as a sharding finding and retracted it when the 1k control contradicted it.
- Concurrent load. The reported run had the machine to itself; an earlier run alongside vitest/tsc was discarded.

Remaining candidates for lane 02 to check: the per-event fsync (atomic temp-write + fsync + rename per event), the admission_log insert on every append, and anything on the append path that re-reads growing state.

Reproduce: npx tsx scripts/measure/corpus.ts --tiers 1000,2000,4000,8000,16000
Re-render the doc without re-measuring: --from-json <raw.json>

Also in the report: storage is ~1.32 KB/event (pretty-printed JSON event files — an upper bound; a compact encoding would cut it materially), and rebuild from durable events reproduces the projection digest exactly at every tier.
summary: F-APPEND-GROWTH (lane 02): EventStore.append p50 grows as n^0.50 with corpus size — p95 crosses C28 A25's 100 ms durable-capture target at ~35k events
